Collectively, the team combines qualitative customer research with deep commercial analytics to evaluate competitor models, diagnose performance gaps across the end-to-end booking journey, and define high-value opportunities that scale effectively across borders. Scope Cover CSA works and associated quality records across the assigned regional portfolio, including new build, fit-out and external works. Maintain inspection templates, audit arrangements and evidence requirements aligned with CTS procedures, approved designs and project specifications. Key CSA Experience Experience should cover the following areas, as applicable to the assigned project scope: Civil works: earthworks, formation and compaction, piling and foundations, underground drainage and services, roads, slabs and hardstanding. Concrete: reinforcement, cover, formwork, embedded items and anchor bolts, placement, compaction, curing, test records, surveys and controlled repairs. Structural works: steelwork and precast installation, connections, welding and bolting records, tolerances, grouting and protective coatings. Building envelope: roofing, cladding, waterproofing, insulation, air and vapour barriers, seals and specified performance testing. Architectural works: partitions, ceilings, doors, raised floors, floor finishes, coatings and workmanship standards. Passive fire protection: compartmentation, firestopping, fire doors and structural fire protection, including installation traceability and inspection before concealment. MEP interfaces: openings, penetrations, builders' work, equipment bases, access provisions, room condition and cleanliness for area handover. Key Accountabilities Own the regional CSA audit plan, with site visits and surveillance targeted at project risk, critical activities and recurring defects. Audit subcontractor quality plans, Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs) and inspection arrangements to confirm they are in place before relevant work starts. Verify that site teams establish benchmarks and first-of-kind installations, obtain the required acceptance and use them to maintain workmanship standards. Check that hold and witness points are planned, notified and recorded, and that required releases are obtained from the authorised parties before work proceeds. Prioritise work that will become inaccessible, including concrete pours, backfilling, enclosed cavities, firestopping and building-envelope interfaces. Issue clear audit findings against the applicable requirements. Agree action owners and due dates and verify closeout using objective evidence. Challenge recurring defects and non-conformance reports (NCRs), require root-cause investigation and check that corrective actions prevent recurrence across projects. Escalate significant quality risks and overdue actions to project leadership and the Head of Quality. Recommend work holds where required under agreed project procedures. Check that project programmes allow time for inspections, internal and client walkdowns, snagging, repairs and verification before area handover. Report regional performance, repeat defects and emerging risks to the Head of Quality, with clear actions and support required. Core Responsibilities Run weekly or fortnightly quality reviews with site teams covering audit actions, NCRs, inspection status, upcoming hold points and handover constraints. Coach site teams, share practical lessons and issue quality bulletins to improve inspection quality and prevent repeat problems. Site teams and subcontractors remain responsible for carrying out the work, day-to-day inspections, corrective actions and maintaining their records. The Regional CSA Quality Lead checks that the required approvals and evidence are in place and escalates unresolved concerns. Ability to interpret drawings, specifications and approved submittals, identify departures from requirements and support evidence-based resolution. Experience planning and conducting construction audits, investigating NCRs, verifying corrective actions and reporting trends across projects. Working knowledge of quality management systems and ISO 9001 principles. Internal or Lead Auditor training, or equivalent, is desirable. Confident using ACC/BIM 360 or equivalent systems for inspections, issues, document control and handover evidence. Clear communication and the confidence to challenge weak evidence, coach site teams and follow actions through to verified closure. Experience across multiple sites or international projects is desirable, with flexibility to travel frequently across the assigned region, including Scandinavia Measures of Success Audit actions and NCRs closed within agreed dates, supported by verified evidence. Fewer repeat defects and improved inspection acceptance at the first submission. Required inspections and hold-point releases completed before works are covered or progressed.
